add_paragraph: Priya is tracing what roots actually release. Her PhD follows the exudates that leak from living roots into the soil around them — sugars, organic acids, amino acids — and asks how a temperature that swings, rather than one that simply rises, changes what the microbial community gets to eat.

She works on the lab's warming experiment at Station Nord-03, where the plots have been held at +4 °C (steady) and +4 °C (variable) since 2019. The comparison is the point of her thesis: **variability may matter more than the mean**.
Before the lab she spent a year as a research assistant in Lisbon, sieving and running carbon analyses until she knew the method well enough to distrust it.
